question: Refer to the exhibit. An engineer is configuring VXLAN between Core Switch A/B and Router A/B. Router A has been partially configured with: feature vn-segment-vlan-based; feature nv overlay; vlan 10 with vn-segment 10010; and interface Loopback0 with ip address 10.10.0.1/32 and ip pim sparse-mode. Which configuration completes the NVE interface setup on Router A?
context:
feature vn-segment-vlan-based
feature nv overlay
vlan 10
  vn-segment 10010
interface Loopback0
  ip address 10.10.0.1/32
  ip pim sparse-mode
options: interface nve1 / no shutdown / source-interface lo0 / member vni 10010 / no mcast-group
interface nve1 / shutdown / source-interface lo0 / member vni 10010 mcast-group 231.1.1.1
interface nve1 / no shutdown / source-interface lo0 / member vni 10010 mcast-group 231.1.1.1
interface nve1 / no shutdown / source-interface vlan10 / member vni 10010 mcast-group 231.1.1.1
theory: The NVE (Network Virtualization Edge) interface is what actually instantiates the VTEP function; it must be administratively enabled with no shutdown (a shut NVE interface never encapsulates or decapsulates VXLAN traffic), sourced from the loopback already running PIM sparse-mode and reachable via the underlay routing protocol, and it must map the VLAN's vn-segment to a specific VNI member along with an underlay multicast group so BUM traffic for that VNI is replicated via PIM in the transport network. Omitting the multicast-group would leave the VTEP with no way to flood traffic to other VTEPs sharing that VNI, and sourcing from a VLAN SVI instead of the loopback would tie VTEP reachability to a single VLAN's spanning tree state rather than a stable routed loopback. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 3 — VXLAN NVE Interface and Multicast Underlay)
